name: Serve a company enrichment API from n8n with Bright Data and GPT-5.6

parameters.content:
## A company enrichment endpoint your other tools can call

POST a domain, get a company profile back on the same connection. This is an **API**, not a batch job - your CRM, a Clay column, a Zapier step or a one-line `curl` can call it the moment a lead appears.

### How it works

The Webhook Trigger accepts `{ "domain": "acme.com" }` as JSON, form-encoded, or `?domain=acme.com` on the query string, so almost anything can call it without special handling. A bad or missing domain gets a **400** with a readable message rather than a broken profile.

Three Bright Data lookups then run at once: their site, their pricing page, and a web search for who they are. Each is parsed for the things worth having - positioning, plan names and figures, employee and funding hints, recent headlines. GPT-5.6 writes a one-paragraph summary from those findings only.

The response is a fixed JSON shape every time, including `checks` saying which lookups actually succeeded. A caller that has to guess which keys exist this time cannot use an API at all.

### Setup

1. Bright Data: a Web Unlocker zone and a SERP zone, as one Header Auth credential.

2. An OpenAI credential.

3. Activate the workflow and copy the **Production URL** from the Webhook node.

4. Call it: `curl -X POST <url> -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"domain":"stripe.com"}'`

## 1. Someone calls the endpoint
JSON, form-encoded or a query string. A caller should not have to know which one this workflow prefers.

## 2. Is it even a domain?
A typo becomes three Bright Data calls and a confident profile of nothing. This is where that stops, with a readable 400.

## 3. Three lookups, at once
Their site, their pricing page and what the web says. None waits for the others and any one can come back empty.

## 4. Read each answer
Positioning and product signals from the site, plans and figures from the pricing page, profiles and coverage from the search.

## 5. One fixed shape
Every field exists on every response, and `checks` says which lookups worked. A caller cannot branch on keys that come and go.

## 6. A paragraph a human can read
Written from the findings only. If the site could not be read, it says so instead of describing a company it cannot see.

## 7. Answer on the same connection
Respond to Webhook closes the loop the caller opened. This is the node that makes it an API rather than a pipeline.

## Put something in front of this before it is public

A webhook URL is a URL. Anyone who has it can call it, and every call spends your Bright Data and OpenAI quota - so an endpoint that is shared casually is a bill somebody else is running up.

The Webhook node has **Authentication** built in: set it to Header Auth and give callers a key. That is one dropdown and it is the difference between an internal tool and an open one.

Also worth knowing: this answers in about 10-25 seconds because it is doing three live fetches. That is fine for a server-to-server call and too slow for a synchronous UI - if a user is waiting, call it in the background and show the result when it lands.

={{ JSON.stringify({ zone: $('Settings').first().json.unlocker_zone, url: $('Read The Request').first().json.pricing_url, format: 'raw', data_format: 'markdown' }) }}

={{ JSON.stringify({ zone: $('Settings').first().json.serp_zone, url: 'https://www.google.com/search?q=' + encodeURIComponent($('Read The Request').first().json.search_query) + '&gl=' + encodeURIComponent($('Settings').first().json.search_country) + '&brd_json=1', format: 'json' }) }}
